It is the [[List of South African airports by passenger movements|second-busiest airport in the country]] and [[List of busiest airports in Africa|fourth-busiest in Africa]]. Located approximately {{convert|20|km|mi}} from the [[Cape Town CBD]] (the city's main economic hub), the airport was opened in 1954 to replace Cape Town's previous airport, [[Wingfield Aerodrome]]. Cape Town International Airport is the only airport in the [[City of Cape Town|Cape Town metropolitan area]] that offers scheduled passenger services. The airport has domestic and international terminals, linked by a common central terminal. The airport has [[direct flight]]s from South Africa's other two main urban areas, [[Johannesburg]] and [[Durban]], as well as flights to smaller centres in South Africa. Internationally, it has direct flights to several destinations in [[Africa]], and locations in the [[Middle East]], [[Asia]], [[Europe]], [[South America]], [[Australia]], and the [[United States]]. The air route between Cape Town and Johannesburg was the world's ninth-busiest air route in 2011 with an estimated 4.5 million passengers.{{cite news|last=The Economist|first=Online|title=Top Flights|url=https://www.economist.com/blogs/graphicdetail/2012/05/daily-chart-8|newspaper=The Economist|access-date=6 June 2012|date=14 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120605193426/http://www.economist.com/blogs/graphicdetail/2012/05/daily-chart-8|archive-date=5 June 2012|url-status=live}} According to [[Airports Company South Africa]], CTIA achieved an on-time performance (OTP) of 90.42% in 2025; above its target.{{cite web|url= https://www.thesouthafrican.com/travel/acsas-latest-stats-most-on-time-airports-airlines-south-africa/ |title= ACSA's latest stats reveal the most on-time SA airlines and airports |author= Sundeeka Mungroo |publisher= The South African |date= 13 October 2025 |access-date= 26 October 2025 }} In 2025, Cape Town International was ranked as the Best Airport in the World in the ''AirHelp Score'' list, moving up one spot from the previous year. Based on visitor opinions, the airport performed particularly well in the categories of on-time performance and customer experience.{{cite web|url= https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/cape-town-international-airport-ranked-best-airport-in-the-world/ |title= Cape Town International Airport ranked best airport in the world |author= SABC News |publisher= SABC News |date= 12 July 2025 |access-date= 13 July 2025 }}{{cite web|url= https://www.capetownetc.com/things-to-do-cape-town/travel/cape-town-international-airport-awarded-title-of-best-airport-globally/ |title= Cape Town International Airport awarded title of best airport globally |author= Sibuliso Duba |publisher= CapeTown ETC |date= 12 July 2025 |access-date= 13 July 2025 }} ==History== '''[[D. F. Malan]] Airport''' was opened in 1954, a year after Jan Smuts Airport (now [[O. R. Tambo International Airport]]) on the [[Witwatersrand]], near Johannesburg, opened. The airport replaced Cape Town's previous airport, [[Wingfield Aerodrome]]. Originally named Bellville Airport due to its proximity to the town of the [[Bellville, South Africa|same name]], it initially served as a domestic airport. Then, at the request of the Bellville Federation of Taxpayers, the airport was renamed after the [[Daniel François Malan|then South African prime minister]]. D.F. Malan National Airport soon achieved international airport status when a direct flight to [[Great Britain|Britain]] and a second flight to Britain via [[Johannesburg]] was introduced. {{cite web |title=Sinking of Borehole, Bellville Airport Construction|last=Lister Pike|first=C|year=1947|publisher=Geological Survey|location=Cape Town|url=https://www.dws.gov.za/ghreport/reports/GH0080.pdf}} {{cite book |title=Cape Town in the twentieth century: an illustrated social history |last=Bickford-Smith |first=Vivian |author2=E. Van Heyningen |author3=Nigel Worden |year=1999 |publisher=New Africa Books |location=Cape Town |isbn=978-0-86486-384-3 |page=120 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SkxmcdhpPbMC}} With the fall of [[apartheid]] in the early 1990s, ownership of the airport was transferred from the state to the newly formed [[Airports Company South Africa]],{{cite web|url=http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=67 |title=ACSA – History |publisher=Airports Company South Africa |access-date=28 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720010851/http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=67 |archive-date=20 July 2011 }} and the airport was renamed to the politically neutral Cape Town International Airport.{{cite web |url=http://cape-townairport.co.za/ |title=Cape Town Airport (CPT) Information – Airports Guide to Cape Town |publisher=airports-guides.com |access-date=28 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130328061437/http://cape-townairport.co.za/ |archive-date=28 March 2013 |url-status=live }} [[South African Airways]] launched a route to Miami in December 1992.{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/90052843/the-orlando-sentinel/ | title=Trip tips: Bulletin board | work=The Orlando Sentinel | date=13 December 1992 | accessdate=4 December 2021 | page=H-1}} In January 2000, the carrier replaced it with a flight to Atlanta, whose outbound leg from Cape Town included a stop in Fort Lauderdale.{{cite news | title=S. African flights arriving soon | work=South Florida Sun Sentinel | date=January 27, 2000 | author=Stieghorst, Tom | pages=[https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87646541/ 1D], [https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87646629/ 2D]}} The first years of the twenty-first century saw tremendous growth at the airport; from handling 6.2 million passengers per annum in 2004–05, the airport peaked at 8.4 million passengers per annum in 2007–08 before falling back to 7.8 million in 2008–09.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} In June 2008, [[Delta Air Lines]] started a flight to New York via Dakar. The motion was unsuccessful.{{Cite web |url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2019-03-05-anc-shoots-down-eff-plan-to-rename-cape-town-airport-after-mama-winnie/ |title=ANC shoots down EFF plan to rename Cape Town airport after Mama Winnie |work=TimesLIVE |date=5 March 2019 |access-date=6 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306071920/https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2019-03-05-anc-shoots-down-eff-plan-to-rename-cape-town-airport-after-mama-winnie/ |archive-date=6 March 2019 |url-status=live }} In February 2021, the [[Cape Times]] reported that the proposed name change of the airport had been "quietly ditched".{{Cite web|last=Villette|first=Francesca|date=26 February 2021|title=Cape Town airport name change ditched|url=https://www.iol.co.za/capetimes/news/cape-town-airport-name-change-ditched-c429ca41-b5d0-45c6-b70f-42f70f8226dd|url-status=live|access-date=2021-03-16|website=www.iol.co.za|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226053752/https://www.iol.co.za/capetimes/news/cape-town-airport-name-change-ditched-c429ca41-b5d0-45c6-b70f-42f70f8226dd |archive-date=26 February 2021 }} In 2024, CTIA experienced its highest tourism passenger volumes on record. During 2024, the airport processed over 10 million passengers and 75,000 tons of cargo.{{cite web|url= https://www.2oceansvibe.com/1-lifestyle/sub-cape-town-international-airport-is-doing-so-well-theres-a-call-for-urgent-upgrades/ |title= Cape Town International Airport Is Doing So Well, There's A Call For Urgent Upgrades |author= |publisher= 2 Oceans Vibe |date= 2 October 2025 |access-date= 2 October 2025 }} Despite this, in early 2025, the airport reported even higher transit figures, with an 8% increase in domestic travel, a 5% increase in international arrivals, and a 56% increase in cargo volumes. In October 2025, it was reported that, based on recent air travel statistics, numerous airlines were choosing to send an increasing number of outbound flights from SA via Cape Town International instead of via Johannesburg's O. R. Tambo International. Reasons include greater efficiency with immigration processing and reduced layover times in Cape Town, compared to Johannesburg.{{cite web|url= https://www.travelnews.co.za/article/outbound-travellers-increasingly-bypass-jnb |title= Outbound travellers increasingly bypass JNB |author= Tylin Moodley |publisher= travelnews |date= 6 October 2025 |access-date= 7 October 2025 }} In March 2026, it was reported that an increasing number of foreign passengers were choosing to travel via Cape Town International, rather than landing at O.R. Tambo (in Johannesburg), when visiting South Africa. CTIA's passenger numbers more than doubled between 2012 and 2026, whereas Joburg's have decreased during the same period. Similarly, while O.R. Tambo's total aircraft figures were roughly the same in 2026 as they were in 2012, those at Cape Town International had tripled over that period. Furthermore, there has been an increase over that period of the number of passengers (average capacity) carried by planes landing at CTIA.{{cite web|url= https://www.news24.com/life/travel/foreign-travellers-are-ditching-joburgs-or-tambo-for-direct-cape-town-flights-20260325-0965 |title= Foreign travellers are ditching Joburg's OR Tambo for direct Cape Town flights |author= Andrew Thompson |publisher= news24 |date= 26 March 2026 |access-date= 27 March 2026 }} In July 2026, Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) confirmed that the development of a large-scale [[solar power]] plant at Cape Town International was well underway. The project is set to have a peak generation capacity of at least 2.5 megawatts (MWp), with the goal of reducing the airport's reliance on the national grid, while also reducing operating costs and carbon emissions. ACSA said airports needed to make these kind of infrastructure investments. Following similar developments at airports in George, Kimberley, and Upington, Cape Town International will become SA's first major airport (international gateway) to have this kind of off-grid power setup.{{cite web|url= https://www.capetownetc.com/news/cape-town-international-airport-advances-major-solar-power-project/ |title= Cape Town International Airport advances major solar power project |author= Lulama Klassen |publisher= Cape Town ETC |date= 13 July 2026 |access-date= 16 July 2026 }} == Infrastructure development == === 2010 upgrades === [[File:2011-02-08_15-08-48_South_Africa_-_Crossroads.jpg|thumb|Apron view]] [[File:2013.01.03 Ciudad del Cabo, ZA (28).JPG|thumb|Check-in hall]] [[File:Cape Town International Airport Departures Area.jpg|thumb|Local and international departures area on the upper floor of the Central Terminal.]] [[File:International Departures, Cape Town Airport.jpg|thumb|Interior of the international terminal|alt=]] In preparation for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], Cape Town International Airport was extensively expanded and renovated. The main focus was the development of a Central Terminal Building at a cost of R1.6 billion,{{cite news |title=New terminal hailed as a success |url=http://www.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1&click_id=13&art_id=vn20091108075550577C968736 |first=Zara |last=Nicholson |newspaper=Sunday Argus |publisher=IOL |date=8 November 2009 |access-date=28 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091124215120/http://www.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1&click_id=13&art_id=vn20091108075550577C968736 |archive-date=24 November 2009 |url-status=live }} which linked the formerly separate domestic and international terminals and provided a common check-in area.{{cite web|url=http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=3785 |title=ACSA – New Developments |publisher=Airports Company South Africa |access-date=28 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720010916/http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=3785 |archive-date=20 July 2011 }} The departures level of the Central Terminal opened in November 2009, with the entire building opened in April 2010. Apart from the now-completed 2010 expansion project, it had been proposed that a second runway for large aircraft be constructed at the airport, to be completed by 2015. However, this second runway has not been constructed. In May 2015, [[Airports Company South Africa]] announced a R7.7 billion expansion for the airport. The expansion includes the upgrades of the Domestic & International terminals. The expansion has been postponed indefinitely due to the drop in passenger numbers due to the global [[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa|COVID-19 pandemic]] from 2020.{{Cite web |url=https://www.iol.co.za/capetimes/news/covid-grounds-r7bn-cape-town-airport-expansion-9c83db24-db5b-440e-bff0-84ee7915e59e |title=Covid grounds R7bn Cape Town airport expansion |date=2022-02-10 |publisher=Independent Online |access-date=2022-06-01}} === 2027 developments === In February 2026, [[Airports Company South Africa]] (ACSA) announced a R10.14 billion upgrade project for Cape Town International. As part of the project, CTIA (which at the time was SA's fastest-growing airport) would receive upgrades in phases, over a number of years. Renovations would take place on the domestic and international terminals, starting in April 2027. Furthermore, a new, realigned main runway would be constructed, with contractor appointment for that part of the project planned for December 2026.{{cite web|url= https://www.moneyweb.co.za/news/economy/acsa-finally-reveals-r10bn-overhaul-of-cape-town-international-airport/ |title= Acsa finally reveals R10bn overhaul of Cape Town International Airport |author= Suren Naidoo |publisher= Moneyweb |date= 20 February 2026 |access-date= 21 February 2026 }} Other parts of the massive infrastructure project include additional domestic contact gates and airbridges, expanded apron capacity to support increased aircraft parking and improved aircraft movement flow, additional international apron stands, expanded commercial and lounge offerings, and improvements to immigration processing and bussing gates. The project's goals were to enhance passenger processing capacity, improve circulation of passengers, and modernize the overall terminal environment in line with a projected growth in demand at CTIA. Its total cost represented over half of ACSA's then-current R21.7 billion overall [[Capital expenditure|capex]] budget for all of the airports it managed. At the time of the announcement, Thabo Phateng, acting regional general manager of CTIA, said that the developments represented a significant step in strengthening Cape Town International Airport's role as a critical economic gateway for both the Western Cape and South Africa. He further stated that by expanding capacity and enhancing operational resilience, the airport is being positioned to support sustained passenger growth, tourism expansion, trade facilitation, and long term regional economic development. ==Facilities== ===Terminals=== The airport has two terminals linked together by one central terminal. ====Central Terminal==== The terminal building has a split-level design, with departures located on the upper floors and arrivals in the lower floors; an elevated roadway system provides vehicular access to both departures and arrivals levels. All check-in takes place within the Central Terminal Building, which contains 120 check-in desks and 20 self-service kiosks. Passengers then pass through a consolidated security screening area before dividing. Passengers flying internationally head to the northern part of the airport which is the international terminal, and passengers flying to other parts of South Africa head to the southern part of the airport to the domestic terminal. The terminal has 10 air bridges, evenly split between domestic and international usage. Sections of lower levels of the domestic and international terminals are used for transporting passengers via bus to and from remotely parked aircraft. Arriving passengers collect luggage in the old sections of their respective terminals, before proceeding through new passageways to the new Central Terminal Building. The terminal contains an automated [[baggage handling system]], capable of handling 30,000 bags per hour. Retail outlets are located on the lower (arrivals) level of the terminal at [[Landside#Airport structures|landside]], as well as [[Airside (airport)|airside]] at the departure gates. Retail outlets are diverse, including foreign exchange services, bookstores, clothing retailers, grocery stores, souvenir outlets and [[Duty-free shop|duty-free]] in international departures. Restaurants within the terminal building are located on the upper (3rd) level above the departures level, and include [[Ocean Basket]], [[Mugg & Bean]], [[Primi Cafe]], [[Wimpy (restaurant)|Wimpy]],{{cite web |url= https://capetown-internationalairport.co.za/airport/facilities-food-drink.html |title= Facilities - Food and Drink |author= |publisher= ZAirports |date= |access-date= 1 January 2025 |archive-date= 1 January 2025 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250101070507/https://capetown-internationalairport.co.za/airport/facilities-food-drink.html |url-status= live }} and what is purported to be the largest [[Spur Steak Ranches|Spur restaurant]] on the African continent, at {{convert|1080|m2|sqft|abbr=on}}. The restaurant level overlooks the [[Airside (airport)|airside]] of the terminal, where a glass [[curtain wall (architecture)|curtain wall]] separates the patrons from the planes three stories below. On the 4th floor is where the airport's lounges are situated. The [[Bidvest Group|Bidvest]], as well as [[South African Airways]] lounges, can be found there, as well as a [[Woolworths (South Africa)|Woolworths Food]] store. ====International Terminal==== [[File:Cape Town International Airport.jpg|thumb|Terminals seen from apron]] The international terminal is located on the northern side of the airport. Customs and Immigration facilities, lounges, duty-free shops, restaurants, prayer rooms, conference rooms, airline offices, and chapels are located in the terminal. ====Domestic Terminal==== Located on the southern side of the airport, it has the same facilities as the international terminal, with the exception of Immigration facilities. ===Other facilities=== There are two hotels located within the airport precinct: Hotel Verde, a four-star hotel owned by Bon Hotels and ranked as "Africa's greenest hotel",{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/travel/hotels/best-airport-hotels-in-world-moxy-naumi-radisson-blu-a8236156.html|title=These are the 10 best airport hotels in the world|date=2 March 2018|work=The Independent|language=en-GB|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312204714/http://www.independent.co.uk/travel/hotels/best-airport-hotels-in-world-moxy-naumi-radisson-blu-a8236156.html|archive-date=12 March 2018|url-status=live}} and the other being Road Lodge, a budget hotel owned by the City Lodge hotel chain group. An [[ExecuJet Aviation Group|ExecuJet]] facility is located near the southern end of the main runway and caters for business jets. ==Airlines and destinations== During its peak [[Tourism|tourist]] (South Africa)|N2]] freeway, with Airport Approach Road providing a direct link between the N2 (at exit 16) and the airport. The airport can also be indirectly accessed from the [[R300 (Western Cape)|R300]] freeway via the [[M12 (Cape Town)|M12]], [[M10 (Cape Town)|M10]] and [[M22 (Cape Town)|M22]].{{Citation needed|date=December 2024}} The airport provides approximately 1,424 parking spaces in the general parking area, and 1,748 parking bays in the multi-storey car park located near the domestic terminal.{{cite web|url=http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=3637 |title=ACSA – Cape Town – Maps and parking |publisher=Airports Company South Africa |access-date=28 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113093904/http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=3637 |archive-date=13 November 2008 }} A new car park opened in 2010, which is located near the international terminal and provides an additional 4,000 parking spaces.{{cite news|title=More parking comes online at Cape Town International Airport |newspaper=Airports Company South Africa |date=10 December 2009 |url=http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=94&toolid=2&itemid=6386 |access-date=28 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720011009/http://www.acsa.co.za/home.asp?pid=94&toolid=2&itemid=6386 |archive-date=20 July 2011 }} The airport also offers a valet parking service. ===Public transport=== Transport to and from the airport is provided by metered taxis, [[e-hailing]] services (such as [[Uber]] and [[Bolt (company)|Bolt]]), and various private shuttle companies. The airport features a dedicated "drop & go" area for taxis and carpooling. ===Rail link=== There is no direct rail access to Cape Town International Airport. In 2013, the [[Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa]] (PRASA) proposed a {{convert|4|km|mi|abbr=on}} rail link between the airport and Cape Town's existing [[Metrorail Western Cape|suburban rail network]], however this has not yet been developed.{{Cite web |date=2013-08-01 |title=Cape Town/Durban airports rail links explored {{!}} Freight News |url=https://www.freightnews.co.za/article/cape-towndurban-airports-rail-links-explored |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.freightnews.co.za |language=en}} ==Accolades== In 2025, Cape Town International was ranked as the best airport in the world in the ''AirHelp Score'' list, shifting from its 2024 rank of second-best. Based on visitor opinions, the airport performed particularly well in the categories of on-time performance and customer experience. In the same year, CTIA was ranked the Best Airport in Africa, Best Airport Staff Service in Africa, and Cleanest Airport in Africa, in the ''2025 Skytrax World Airport Awards''. The award is based on Skytrax's customer satisfaction study, across 575 airports in 100 countries.{{cite web|url= https://businesstech.co.za/news/business/820394/two-south-african-airports-ranked-among-the-best-in-the-world/ |title= Two South African airports ranked among the best in the world |author= Staff Writer |publisher= BusinessTech |date= 10 April 2025 |access-date= 2 October 2025 }} In 2026, CTIA was named Africa's Best Airport for the 11th consecutive year, at the annual Skytrax World Airport Awards.{{cite web|url= https://topauto.co.za/features/147801/south-african-airport-named-the-best-in-africa/ |title= South African airport named the best in Africa |author= Warren Hawkins |publisher= TopAuto |date= 5 April 2026 |access-date= 6 April 2026 }} == Accidents and incidents == * On 7 November 2007, [[Nationwide Airlines Flight 723]], a [[Boeing 737-200]], had its right hand engine detach from the airframe during [[Rotation (aeronautics)|rotation]]. The pilots declared an emergency and safely landed at the airport saving all 112 occupants onboard without injury.{{Cite web |last=Ranter |first=Harro |title=Serious incident Boeing 737-230 ZS-OEZ, Wednesday 7 November 2007 |url=https://asn.flightsafety.org/wikibase/321836 |access-date=2024-12-22 |website=asn.flightsafety.org |archive-date=21 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250221160333/https://asn.flightsafety.org/wikibase/321836 |url-status=live }} ==See also== * [[List of airports in South Africa]] * [[List of South African airports by passenger movements]] ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons category-inline|Cape Town International Airport}} * [https://www.airports.co.za/airports/cape-town-international-airport Official website] {{Portal bar|South Africa|Aviation}} {{Cape Town|transport}} {{Passenger airports of South Africa}} {{African Airports TOP 10}} {{National Key Points navbox}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Transport in Cape Town]] [[Category:Airports in South Africa]] [[Category:Airports established in 1954]] [[Category:1954 establishments in South Africa]] [[Category:Visitor centers in South Africa]]

Cape Town  International Airport (IATA: CPT, ICAO: FACT), and sometimes abbreviated to CTIA, is the primary international airport serving the city of Cape Town, South Africa. It is the second-busiest airport in the country and fourth-busiest in Africa.
Located approximately 20 kilometres (12 mi) from the Cape Town CBD (the city's main economic hub), the airport was opened in 1954 to replace Cape Town's previous airport, Wingfield Aerodrome. Cape Town International Airport is the only airport in the Cape Town metropolitan area that offers scheduled passenger services.  The airport has domestic and international terminals, linked by a common central terminal.
The airport has direct flights from South Africa's other two main urban areas, Johannesburg and Durban, as well as flights to smaller centres in South Africa.  Internationally, it has direct flights to several destinations in Africa, and locations in the Middle East, Asia, Europe, South America, Australia, and the United States.
The air route between Cape Town and Johannesburg was the world's ninth-busiest air route in 2011 with an estimated 4.5 million passengers.
According to Airports Company South Africa, CTIA achieved an on-time performance (OTP) of 90.42% in 2025; above its target.
In 2025, Cape Town International was ranked as the Best Airport in the World in the AirHelp Score list, moving up one spot from the previous year. Based on visitor opinions, the airport performed particularly well in the categories of on-time performance and customer experience.
